text:
Kate M.: Heads up — ACME reported p99 latency jumps ~2x starting ~10m after the v2.11.0 runtime canary went live. p95 up ~30%. They’re seeing timeouts on long-context requests. Raising to eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout v2.11.0 -> 10% traffic to runtime-pool-canary-7 started at 2025-11-03T15:12:30Z :rocket:

Alex T.: noted. can someone paste the canary host list? I’ll check kv-cache metrics and tail slow requests.

Priya S.: canary node pool: canary-7a, canary-7b. Metrics: total qps steady, p50 unchanged, p95 +28%, p99 +95%. Linking charts: https://grafana.redwood/shot/rt/p95_vs_time (internal) :eyes:

Marc C.: checked logs on canary-7a — bursts of "kv-cache miss" followed by long kernel queuing around 15:22. Example request id: req_3f9a1c (attached log snippet).

Marc C.: log snippet:
```
[2025-11-03T15:22:11Z] req=req_3f9a1c model=gpt-large seq=4096 latency=4200ms state=KV_CACHE_MISS queuing=3800ms
[2025-11-03T15:22:11Z] worker=worker-12 gpu=0 cu_idle=90% batch_size=1
```

Alex T.: hmm queuing 3.8s — looks like sudden serialization at the executor. Any recent kernel/driver changes on canary nodes?

Priya S.: No infra node image change in the last week. BUT runtime config v2.11.0 enabled "continuous-batching: aggressive" by default and bumped max-batch-wait to 5ms -> 15ms in some builds. That could change batching behavior for very long sequences.

Dan R.: if batching increased, long-seq requests might block KV cache reuse and cause head-of-line blocking. Suggest bisecting the runtime commits between v2.10.4 and v2.11.0 to isolate change.

Lina O.: CS asked for quick mitigation. Options: 1) pause canary rollout (stop traffic to canary-7 pool), 2) rollback to v2.10.4 on canary nodes, or 3) hotfix to revert batching change. Which do we want now? :thinking_face:

Alex T.: I can run a quick traffic-shift to rollback canary to 0%. Command we use: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/runtime-canary runtime=redwood/runtime:v2.10.4 --record` but we also have autoscaler routing flags: `rwctl rollout canary --set-weight 0 --target canary-7` — prefer rwctl to avoid k8s churn.

Priya S.: I’m +1 for immediate traffic shift to 0% while we bisect. That buys time for a proper fix. I’ll open an incident page and set priority P1 for customer impact.

deploy-bot: rwctl: traffic shift to canary-7 -> 0% requested by Priya S. (action started)

Marc C.: after shifting traffic, p95 on ACME cohort dropped back toward baseline within ~45s. Looks like routing mitigation worked. We still need root cause.

Dan R.: For bisect: steps I propose:
1) git checkout v2.10.4
2) git bisect start v2.11.0 v2.10.4
3) iterative test: run stress harness that reproduces p99 with long-context payload (I’ll share the harness).

Dan R.: quick bisect commands:
```
git bisect start v2.11.0 v2.10.4
# run test, mark good/bad
# e.g. ./tools/run_latency_test --model gpt-large --seq 4096 --concurrency 8
git bisect good|bad
```

Alex T.: I’ll run the harness against each bisect candidate on a small private pool. FYI the reproducer: curl to /v1/generate with header `X-RW-Test: long-seq` and payload tokens ~4096. We measure p99 over 50 requests.

Priya S.: Also add tracing span sampling for canary hosts: enable 100% traces for a short window so we can inspect KV cache lifecycle and kernel queuing. `tracectl set-sample canary-7 1.0 --duration 10m`

Marc C.: Early bisect candidate shows commit 8f3b2a which touched `batcher.cc` (changed scheduling loop). Reproducer on that build shows p99 spike consistent with customer.

Dan R.: confirmed — commit 8f3b2a introduces a different wake/sleep policy to reduce CPU wakeups but accidentally increases batch-hold time under low QPS long-seq scenarios. Patch idea: respect max-latency-per-request cap for long-seq paths (avoid holding batch waiting for more requests). I’ll draft a quick fix.

Lina O.: once Dan has a patch we should canary it on a single node with telemetry for batch hold times. If patch reduces p99 on the reproducer, we can promote.

Alex T.: After rollback we observed no further customer errors. Kate, can you confirm with ACME that errors reduced?

Kate M.: Confirmed with ACME support: timeouts stopped after you shifted traffic. They’ll keep us posted if anything reappears. Thanks team. :heart:

Priya S.: follow-ups:
- Dan: open PR with regression test (harness + assert on p99 threshold).
- Alex: replayed post-mortem steps in runbook and add a note about the batching flag being risky for long-seq.
- Marc: attach logs and example request ids to the incident page.

Dan R.: PR opened: https://git.redwood/rt/commit/PR-421 (internal). Patch reverts aggressive hold and adds regression test.

Alex T.: once PR merges, we should do a minimal canary (5% on single node) and observe for 30m before broad rollout.

Priya S.: Thanks all. I’ll mark incident P1 -> mitigated and leave open for verification. If anything changes, ping @eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
